requirements.quote: To protect the connection from failing due to such a spurious migration, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails.
requirements.condition: Validation of a new peer address fails.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must revert to using the last validated peer address.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not continue using the failed, unvalidated peer address as its active peer address.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can make validation of a new peer address fail and observe which peer address the endpoint subsequently uses.

requirements.quote: Additionally, receipt of packets with higher packet numbers from the legitimate peer address will trigger another connection migration.
requirements.condition: The endpoint receives packets with higher packet numbers from the legitimate peer address after a spurious migration.
requirements.required_behavior: The receipt must trigger another connection migration.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can deliver higher-numbered packets from the legitimate address and observe whether the endpoint enters connection migration processing.

requirements.quote: This will cause the validation of the address of the spurious migration to be abandoned
requirements.condition: Higher-numbered packets from the legitimate peer address trigger another connection migration while the spurious migration address is being validated.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must abandon validation of the address associated with the spurious migration.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not continue validating the spurious migration address after the legitimate-address migration is triggered.
requirements.why_checkable: The required state transition follows directly from the adjacent description and can be checked by observing whether validation of the spurious address remains active.

requirements.quote: If an endpoint has no state about the last validated peer address, it MUST close the connection silently by discarding all connection state.
requirements.condition: The endpoint has no state about the last validated peer address.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must silently close the connection and discard all connection state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not retain the connection as active or emit a connection-close response as part of this silent closure.
requirements.error_behavior: Close the connection silently by discarding all connection state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can remove or omit last-validated-address state, induce the relevant failure path, and verify silent closure and complete state removal.

requirements.quote: This results in new packets on the connection being handled generically.
requirements.condition: The endpoint has silently closed the connection by discarding all connection state.
requirements.required_behavior: Subsequent packets for the former connection must be handled generically rather than as packets belonging to retained connection state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not process subsequent packets using discarded connection-specific state.
requirements.why_checkable: The behavior is a directly stated consequence of discarding all connection state and can be tested by sending another packet after closure.

requirements.quote: For instance, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets.
requirements.condition: Further packets arrive after the endpoint has silently closed the connection and discarded its state.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted to send a Stateless Reset in response to those packets.
requirements.why_checkable: A conformance test can verify that sending a Stateless Reset in this condition is treated as permitted behavior rather than a protocol violation.
